correctness.rationale: The final claim is precisely for k=F_q, L=F_(q^d), d>=2, R=L+pi M_d(k[[pi]]) on right S=O^(1xd), and the intermediate first layer only. Reduction mod pi gives the L-subspaces of L^2 (q^d+3 embedded modules). The S-trace separates nonrational point modules from S^2; tensoring with F gives GL2(F) matrix centralizer. Any pole in an isomorphism forces a forbidden nonzero k-linear relation alpha+beta*t=0 at nonrational t; equality of lattice indices forces integral det a unit, so isomorphisms coincide exactly with PGL2(k)-orbits. Stabilizers yield rational class q+3, one degree-two class of q^2-q if 2|d, and T regular H=q(q^2-1) classes where T=(q^d-q-epsilon(q^2-q))/H. Independent GF(2^d) PGL2 orbit enumerations for d=2,3,4,5 produced multiplicity lists [2,3], [3,6], [2,3,6,6], [3,6,6,6,6], respectively; finite samples corroborate but do not prove arbitrary q,d. No Frobenius conjugate quotient is used.
